history.dynasty: Yadava (Devgiri); patronage by Hemadri Pant; later Adilshahi land grant
history.period: Deity installed 178 AD per tradition; shrine built 1273 AD by Hemadri Pant under Ramdevray Yadav
history.summary: Shri Kshetra Jwala Narasimha Teerth at Kole Narsimhapur (Walva taluka, Sangli district - NOT Sangli city), on the banks of the Krishna River about 10 km from Uran Islampur, is an ancient Narasimha kshetra with an underground sanctum. Sthala purana: the 16-armed swayambhu deity - one of the largest shaligram idols in the world - appeared before Parashar Muni (father of Vyasa) before the Mahabharata period; unable to bear its blazing form, the sage immersed it in the Krishna. Around 178 AD King Bhimdev of Kundinyapur recovered it from the river (identified where dry kusha grass caught fire) and installed it. The temple is mentioned in the Gurucharitra (adhyaya 15); Samarth Ramdas visited in 1662; Hemadri Pant built the shrine in 1273 AD under Ramdevray Yadav of Devgiri; Adilshah gifted land for the temple in 1726. The sanctum lies 14 ft underground, reached by descending nine steep steps through narrow tunnels that carry Krishna river water. town_description: Kole Narsimhapur is a village in Walva taluka of Sangli district, on the banks of the Krishna River about 10 km from Uran Islampur. A quiet agrarian village, it is known almost entirely for the Jwala Narasimha kshetra, whose underground sanctum and Krishna riverside setting draw devotees of Narasimha from the region.
